comp_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me begin our SOC 2 Type I compliance journey by preparing the account creation for {{vendor}}, our chosen compliance-automation platform. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: our company legal name, primary domain, the corporate email address or SSO provider we want to use for signup, the name/title of the authorized representative who will complete registration, and any organizational details (company size, industry) {{vendor}} typically requests during onboarding.
2. Research {{vendor}}'s signup flow (via their public website) and identify the exact fields required: account/org name, admin email, password or SSO method, billing/plan selection, and terms-of-service acceptance step.
3. Pre-fill a draft of the signup form with the information I provide, noting clearly which fields still need my input (e.g., payment card details, SSO credential entry) — describe these as form fields, not API calls, since no vendor API endpoints are in scope here.
4. Prepare a short checklist summarizing: (a) what account tier/plan looks appropriate for a SOC 2 Type I effort, (b) which Trust Services Criteria and policy templates we'll likely need to enable once inside the platform, and (c) what evidence-collection integrations (cloud provider, HR system, etc.) we should connect first after account creation.
5. Do NOT submit the signup form, accept {{vendor}}'s terms of service, enter payment/billing authorization, or log in with corporate SSO on my behalf — these require my direct action.

When finished, report back with: the pre-filled form draft, the checklist described above, and a clear list of the remaining fields/actions only I can complete. Then stop for human sign-off so I can review, enter credentials/payment, accept terms, and finalize the account myself.

comp_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me complete the 'Connect integrations' step of our SOC 2 Type I setup in {{vendor}}, our compliance automation platform. Please prepare (but do not finalize) the integration connections needed for evidence collection.

First, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account login/workspace details, (2) the list of systems we need connected — typically our cloud provider(s), identity provider, code hosting, HR system, MDM, and ticketing tool, and (3) whether we have any custom/on-prem systems not in the standard catalog.

Then, using my configured credentials, log into {{vendor}} and navigate to its integrations catalog. For each standard system I name, locate the correct integration entry, confirm it uses read-only scopes where offered, and prepare it for connection — filling in any required configuration fields, but stop before triggering the OAuth authorization or credential-grant flow, since that requires my explicit consent per system.

For any custom or on-prem systems not in the catalog, check whether {{vendor}} supports custom connections via a documented API; if so, describe in words how a developer would create and list such connections so evidence can be pushed manually. Draft the specific setup steps for a developer to implement this, but do not execute API calls that grant access.

Produce a checklist listing: each system to connect, the scopes/permissions each integration will request, and which step requires my manual OAuth approval in the {{vendor}} UI. Flag any integration whose required permissions look broader than read-only so I can review them.

When your checklist and draft configurations are ready, present them to me and stop for human sign-off before any authorization is granted or integration is finalized.

comp_001:n3.prompt:
You are helping me generate the initial set of security policies for our SOC 2 Type I journey using {{vendor}}, our compliance automation platform. If you don't already know them, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} account login/workspace details (confirm you can use your configured credentials to access it), (2) our company legal name and domain, and (3) the list of employees/roles who will need to accept policies.

Actions to take:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using your configured credentials.
2. Locate the policy template library and fetch the standard SOC 2 policy set (e.g., Information Security, Access Control, Data Classification, Incident Response, Change Management, Vendor Management, Business Continuity).
3. If {{vendor}} offers a built-in AI assistant, delegate drafting/customization of each policy to it, tailoring placeholders (company name, scope, roles, review cadence) to our details.
4. Set up or confirm version control and an approval workflow within {{vendor}} so each policy has a draft state, an editor history, and a designated approver.
5. Configure per-employee acceptance tracking so the platform will notify staff and log acknowledgments once policies are published.
6. Compile a summary checklist listing every policy generated, its current draft status, assigned approver, and any open placeholders needing my input.

Do not publish, finalize, or mark any policy as approved, and do not trigger employee acceptance notifications. This step requires that a human explicitly approve before changes are applied, so you must stop for human sign-off once drafts and the checklist are ready.

Report back with: the list of policies drafted, a link or path to each in {{vendor}}, the approval workflow status, any unresolved placeholders, and a clear note that you are stopping for human sign-off before publishing.

comp_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the SOC 2 Type I policy set inside Vanta ahead of human compliance review. Do not finalize, publish, or mark any policy as approved—your job is to draft and organize, not to approve.

Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: my company domain, Vanta account access confirmation (assume I use my configured credentials), a description of our actual security practices (e.g., access control model, data handling, incident response process, vendor management, infrastructure/cloud setup), and any existing internal policy documents or wiki pages I want reflected.

Actions to take:
1. Log into Vanta and pull up the default policy templates it generated for our SOC 2 Type I program (e.g., Information Security Policy, Access Control Policy, Data Classification Policy, Incident Response Policy, Vendor Management Policy, etc.).
2. For each policy, compare the template language against the operational details I gave you and draft edits so the wording matches what we actually do (systems used, roles/titles, approval chains, review cadence).
3. Flag any policy sections where the template assumes a control we don't have in place, or where our practice is stricter/looser than the template implies—list these clearly as open questions rather than guessing.
4. Organize your output as a per-policy diff or summary: what Vanta's default said, what you propose changing, and why.

Done looks like: every relevant policy has a drafted redline and a list of unresolved judgment calls, all staged in Vanta as unpublished edits (not applied/approved).

Report back with the full list of policies reviewed, the proposed changes for each, and the open questions needing compliance/legal judgment. Then stop for human sign-off before any policy is approved or applied in Vanta.

comp_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me configure automated compliance tests in {{vendor}} as part of our SOC 2 Type I journey. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account access confirmation (assume you'll use my configured credentials), (2) which systems/integrations are already connected (cloud provider, identity provider, HR system, code repo, etc.), and (3) whether we're scoping to SOC 2 Type I Trust Services criteria only or adding any custom frameworks/controls.

Once you have that, use {{vendor}}'s test listing capability (the equivalent of the 'list tests' API) to pull the current set of automated tests mapped to our connected systems, and identify: which built-in tests are already active, which are failing or need a connection to run, and which controls have no test coverage yet. Where relevant, prepare a summary of any custom controls or custom tests we should add for our own internal policies, including proposed test logic and evidence source in words (no need to write code).

Compile a clear report grouped by: (a) tests already passing, (b) tests failing or blocked pending a system connection, (c) recommended custom tests/controls to add, and (d) any test configuration changes you'd propose (e.g., adjusting schedules, thresholds, or scope).

Do not enable, disable, or modify any test configuration yourself — only prepare the full list of recommended changes with rationale. Present this to me for review and then stop for human sign-off before any changes are applied in {{vendor}}.

comp_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me remediate failing compliance test results in our Vanta SOC 2 Type I monitoring dashboard. Please do the following:

1. If you don't already have it, ask me for access details or confirm you can use my configured credentials to log into Vanta.
2. Pull the current list of failing tests from the Vanta dashboard, grouped by integrated service (e.g., AWS, Google Workspace, GitHub, identity provider, HR system) and by control category (access control, encryption, logging, vulnerability management, etc.).
3. For each failing test, identify the root cause (e.g., MFA not enforced, unencrypted storage bucket, missing log retention policy, inactive user account not deprovisioned, missing vendor security review).
4. Draft a specific remediation plan per failing test: what setting needs to change, in which system, and the exact steps to change it. Where a fix requires a policy document update, draft the revised policy language.
5. Prioritize the list by risk severity and ease of fix, and flag any tests that require a business decision (e.g., choosing a new access policy) rather than a pure technical fix.
6. Compile everything into a single remediation report: test name, current status, root cause, proposed fix, system/owner affected, and estimated effort.

Do not make any configuration changes, update any policies, close out any tests, or mark anything remediated in Vanta yourself. Every change must be explicitly approved by a human before it is applied, since a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied. Prepare the full remediation plan and pre-filled drafts, then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with the complete failing-tests list, your remediation plan for each item, and a clear summary of which items are ready for one-click approval versus which need a policy decision from me first.

comp_001:n7.prompt:
You are helping me operationalize the 'Employee security training' step of our SOC 2 Type I journey in Vanta. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for our Vanta account domain/login context if not already known, our employee roster (or the HR/people-ops source of truth, e.g. Google Workspace, BambooHR, or a spreadsheet I provide), and the deadline I want to set for training completion.
2. Using your configured credentials, log into Vanta and confirm the security training module is enabled and assigned to all current employees and contractors who need it (per our policy scope).
3. Cross-check the Vanta employee list against my roster to flag any missing, duplicate, or offboarded accounts, and prepare a list of discrepancies for me to resolve.
4. Draft a short reminder email/Slack message I can send to employees who haven't completed training yet, including the deadline and a link to the Vanta training portal.
5. Set up a recurring check (daily or every few days, your recommendation) where you poll Vanta's training completion dashboard and report back the current completion percentage, names of employees still pending, and any overdue past the deadline.
6. Note explicitly that actually completing each individual's training modules remains a human step — this is third-party-wait: each employee must log in and finish their own modules on their own schedule, and no agent action can complete that for them.

Done looks like: training assigned to all employees in Vanta, discrepancies list prepared, reminder draft ready, and a monitoring cadence established so I get regular completion-status updates until 100% is reached.

Report back with: current completion %, list of outstanding employees, any roster mismatches found, and the reminder draft text for my review.

comp_001:n8.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to engage a SOC 2 Type I auditor as part of our Vanta compliance journey. This is a policy-gate step: you must prepare everything needed but cannot select a firm, negotiate terms, or sign any engagement letter — that requires an authorized officer's decision.

First, ask me for: (1) our company legal name and domain, (2) our target SOC 2 Type I audit window/deadline if known, (3) whether we have Vanta's list of pre-approved/integrated audit firm partners available, or whether I want you to compile a shortlist of reputable SOC 2 audit firms from public information, and (4) any budget range or firm-size preference (boutique vs. established).

Then do the following:
1. Research and compile a comparison list of 3-5 candidate SOC 2 audit firms (or use Vanta's partner directory if I provide access), including for each: firm name, relevant experience with SOC 2 Type I, typical turnaround time, and general pricing range if publicly available.
2. Draft an outreach email template requesting a proposal/engagement letter from shortlisted firms, referencing our company, desired report type (Type I), and target timeline.
3. Prepare a checklist of information the chosen auditor will likely need from us (system description scope, control list, policy documents, evidence collection status in Vanta).
4. Summarize the shortlist, draft outreach email, and checklist in a single document.

Done looks like: a ready-to-send comparison summary, outreach draft, and information checklist, all pending my review. Do not contact any firm, negotiate pricing, or sign or submit any engagement letter on my behalf — stop for human sign-off once materials are prepared. Report back with the shortlist, drafts, and a clear note that firm selection and contract signature remain my decision to make.

comp_001:n9.prompt:
You are helping me monitor and prepare for the completion of our SOC 2 Type I audit, which we are running through Vanta with an independent third-party auditing firm. The actual conduct and sign-off of the audit examination remains a human step performed by the third-party auditor and cannot be completed or accelerated by you.

First, ask me for anything you need that you don't already have: our company domain, our Vanta account login status (confirm I can access it with my configured credentials), the name of the auditing firm we've engaged (if selected), and the expected audit start/end dates if known.

Then, using my configured credentials, log into our Vanta dashboard and:
1. Check the current audit status (e.g., evidence collection, auditor review, report drafting).
2. Compile a summary of any outstanding evidence requests, failed/at-risk controls, or unresolved policy gaps flagged in Vanta that could delay or block the auditor.
3. Identify any open auditor questions or requests visible in Vanta or via any auditor communication tools we use, and draft clear, factual responses I can review (do not send them yourself).
4. Note the last-updated timestamp on the audit status so we can track progress over time.

Do not sign, approve, submit, or communicate directly with the auditor on my behalf — only prepare drafts and summaries for my review.

Report back with: (a) current audit status and stage, (b) any outstanding items requiring my input or action, (c) drafted responses to auditor requests if any exist, and (d) a recommended date/time for you to poll Vanta again for status updates, since final completion depends on the auditor's independent testing timeline and remains a human step.
